When the price deviates to the extreme Bollinger band and the RSI confirms oversold/overbought, a weak trend (ADX < 20) suggests a mean‑reversion opportunity; this reduces false breakouts in trending markets and improves risk‑adjusted returns.
When price touches a Bollinger band edge, it is likely to revert toward the mean; a low RSI confirms the overextension, and ATR‑based sizing adapts to volatility, improving risk‑adjusted returns.

Bollinger bands capture price volatility envelopes; when price breaches a band and RSI confirms an overbought or oversold condition, the market is likely to revert to the mean, and ATR-based SL/TP scales risk to current volatility.

Tightening the Bollinger bands to 2.2σ captures more reliable mean‑reversion points while the RSI oversold/overbought thresholds (35/65) filter out weak momentum; ATR‑based stops and targets scale risk to current volatility, improving risk‑reward and reducing whipsaw losses.
